input.cause: At the time of both tasks, the procedure schema described the quantities field only as "What the test measures." Nothing told the model to take the quantity and unit from the device's register. The model (claude-sonnet-5-5) named the speed command with quantity Speed and unit percent. The guard refused with UNKNOWN_UNIT: Speed has no unit "percent", and its units are m/s, mm/s, km/h, mi/h and knots. That refusal lists the units of the wrong quantity. It does not say that percent belongs to another quantity or that the register declares the quantity, so the model was misled by a word in the property's name. The rule was not stated in any text the model read (no statement node for the rule was read). The same form also hit the earlier attempt exp-learn/t-2026-09-29-0009 step 17. Since then the description of /properties/quantities was extended to say "the quantity and the unit its register declares; a word of the property's name is not its quantity; physics.units_normalize with the unit alone says which quantity takes a unit". This closes the gap in the text. I did not check whether the refusal message itself changed.

input.summary: Diagnosis diag-f03c4e80df7f accepted by the guard (sha256 c833d29728174717a6e051f648c1c526039b9c20c8cccde3b73c2fb41d131ce7). The lead's reading is right. This is a contract gap. At the time of both tasks (exp4-sonnet-a/t-2026-09-29-0014 step 9 and exp6-contract/t-2026-09-30-0008 step 10), the schema description of /properties/quantities said only "What the test measures." It did not say that the quantity and unit must be the ones the device's register declares. The model named a Speed quantity with the unit "percent" for a scrubber speed command, and the guard refused it with UNKNOWN_UNIT (Speed units are m/s, mm/s, km/h and so on). The checks confirmed that neither task's version of the text held the phrase. The checks also confirmed that today's working tree states it, and that step 10 of exp6 was guard-refused. So the cause is closed in the texts, and the harness can confirm that today. I did not test whether the new wording actually removes the refusal.
